script.title: Composite vs Mixed Supply (CGST)
script.caption_hook: One box, one price. Is the GST rate also one?

lines.say: One box, one price. Is the GST rate also one?
Good question! Bundles are of two types: composite or mixed. Tax differs.
Naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business, like packing and transport. Transport is the principal supply.
Tax follows the principal supply. That's Section 8(a).
Each item can be sold alone, but they're sold together at one price, not naturally bundled. That's mixed.
Like a hamper of chocolates, a candle and a mug?
Exactly! Tax follows the supply with the highest rate. That's Section 8(b). Packed means peak.
Wait... one price always means mixed, right?
Not always. First check natural bundling. Then, if not bundled and one price, take the highest rate. Separate prices? Each taxed separately.
Got it! Natural is principal, packed is peak.
Remember: natural means main, packed means peak.

check_notes: Checker: Line 4 (voice): 'Transport is the principal supply' is wrong. The textbook illustration in Section 2(30) is goods packed, transported and insured, and there the goods are the principal supply. Packing, transport and insurance are only ancillary. Correct: 'Naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business, like goods sent with packing, transport and insurance. The goods are the principal supply, so the whole bundle is taxed at the rate for the goods.'

Checker: Lines 4 and 8 (definitions): composite and mixed supply are defined in Section 2(30) and Section 2(74). Section 8 only sets out how they are taxed. Better: 'Defined in Section 2(30) / 2(74); taxed under Section 8(a) / 8(b).'

Checker: Lines 10, 13 and 14 (mnemonic): 'Packed means peak' is confusing because the composite example in Line 4 is also packed goods. Also, Line 13 says 'Natural is principal' while Line 14 says 'natural means main', so the wording doesn't match. Use one clear version in both places, e.g. 'Natural = Principal, Not natural + single price = Peak (highest rate)'.

Checker: Line 4 (voice): the definition leaves out that a composite supply is two or more taxable supplies, one of which is the principal supply. Add: 'two or more taxable supplies, naturally bundled, one of which is the principal supply'.
reviewer_note: Steps board and the mixed-supply line now reflect Section 2(74): mixed needs single price, items suppliable separately and not naturally bundled. Separately priced non-bundled items are taxed each at its own rate. Please confirm word count (about 160) and the packing-and-transport example.
